form-bind.intro: Continue with the name and price fields declared above; this binds and validates input.

form-output.intro: After successful validation, use form.CleanedData(), not raw input.

form-options.intro: Configure the field before passing it to forms.New.

form-errors.intro: Invalid input returns field errors without saving anything.

model-text-options.intro: The model must declare an exported Name member; the stored column is display_name.

model-clean.intro: Using the name field declared above, clean one value without a database write.

model-null-blank.intro: Nullable permits nil. Optional permits empty input. Neither saves data.

model-choices.intro: Clean rejects values outside Choices. Default describes absent values; it does not make an unknown choice valid.

model-bounds.intro: Set both numeric bounds, then reject an out-of-range input.

model-validator.intro: Return a safe field error from a context-aware validator.

serializer-fields.intro: Only explicitly declared fields are accepted.

serializer-validate.intro: Using the serializer declared above, validate input without saving it.

serializer-output.intro: Use cleaned values from the preceding validation. Representation does not save data.

serializer-directions.intro: Input id is ignored; note is omitted from output. Row authorization is still required.

serializer-partial.intro: Here serializer declares required name and price fields. Partial input skips absent price; it does not authorize a write.

route-handler.intro: Inside an HTTP handler, read the matched id parameter.

route-register.intro: handler is an http.Handler. Include gives the route a catalog namespace.

route-reverse.intro: router contains catalog:detail as defined above. Result: /api/products/42/.

template-loader.intro: Use an in-memory loader for this standalone example.

template-render.intro: engine contains product.html from the loader example. Untrusted description text is escaped.

pagination-config.intro: Accept pages of at most 50 rows.

pagination-parse.intro: pager is configured for page-number pagination. Authorization must be applied before the query.

mail-outbox.intro: This bounded test outbox sends no network email.

mail-send.intro: box is the in-memory outbox above. Result: one simulated message.

signing-config.intro: key must contain a stable, private signing key loaded from settings, not a per-request random key.

signing-token.intro: signer is configured for the catalog-link purpose above.

signing-verify.intro: Verify a token using the same purpose-bound signer. Tampering is rejected.

password-hash.intro: password is submitted input. Never log it; persist only the encoded hash.

password-verify.intro: password and encoded come from the hash example. Verification is not a complete login flow.

session-write.intro: ctx is the HTTP request context after session middleware. A store is required for persistence.

session-read.intro: session is the value loaded above. Read a typed value and check whether it exists.

signal-send.intro: published is the signal declared above. Send invokes connected receivers synchronously.

admin-list.intro: catalog.Product is the showcase model. Configure a site only after completing Admin setup.

admin-search.intro: Continue with the same config. Search, filters and sorting never replace row authorization.

admin-form.intro: Continue with the same config. Readonly values remain visible; slug suggestions are not server defaults.

admin-register.intro: site must already have a scoped store, policy, signer and CSRF settings. config is configured in the preceding examples.

task-options.intro: A pure demo task with no tenant scope. Real tenant work requires current authorization on both producer and worker.

task-register.intro: Use registry and options from the task-options example. The handler honors cancellation and bounds input.

task-delay.intro: double is registered above. client must be fully wired; ctx must have a deadline.

task-result.intro: result is the handle returned by Delay. Wait only on the producer side, never inside a worker.

task-signature.intro: addOne is a registered task that returns input + 1. A signature does not dispatch work.

task-chain.intro: first and next are the signatures above; client is wired with workflow storage and relay.

task-group.intro: first and next are the signatures above; client is wired with workflow storage and relay.

task-retry.intro: Pass options to Register. Explicit Retry requests use this policy; automatic retries require AutoRetryFor.
